result.title: Interpretable many-body interaction laws for collective motion from few trajectories
result.summary: Models of collective motion usually reduce social interactions to pairwise forces, despite empirical evidence for many-body effects. We introduce the directional atomic cluster expansion (dACE), which adapts the atomic cluster expansion (ACE) of interatomic potentials to self-propelled agents. dACE provides a systematically improvable, exactly equivariant expansion of an agent's acceleration that splits uniquely into 1-, 2-, 3-body and higher contributions, along with a self term for the agent's own past motion that is fitted so that it does not absorb the interactions. On simulated collectives in two and three dimensions with known rules, dACE recovers the interaction law body order by body order from little data, while the neural model SocialNet, the current closest competitor, needs more data, has much larger errors on many-body or chiral rules and is restricted to 2D. On real data sets of tracked zebrafish and golden shiners, the laws learned by dACE agree better between disjoint halves of the data than SocialNet's. The learned laws are interpretable, and in the shiners the 3-body term opposes the pairwise response as neighbourhoods get dense. Finally, we show that next-step prediction accuracy mostly measures self-propulsion and noise rather than the interactions, and suggest more robust combinations of error measures for interaction learning.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 directional atomic cluster expansion（dACE），将原子簇展开迁移到自驱动个体，把个体加速度系统可加、严格等变地分解为 1、2、3 体相互作用与自身历史项，并在模拟集群及斑马鱼、金体美鱥追踪数据上恢复可解释的相互作用律。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「自项与多体交互分离、按体阶拆分贡献」的思路，以及「下一步预测精度主要反映自驱动与噪声而非交互」的诊断，可能为 LVR 中 latent 内容的贡献分配与视觉证据是否被真正使用的评价提供可供核查的类比。
